what_it_does: Event cameras are a new kind of image sensor that, instead of taking full frames at fixed intervals, fire tiny signals only when a pixel detects a brightness change — producing a sparse, high-speed stream of events rather than dense video frames. Processing this stream efficiently on a chip is hard because conventional processors expect dense, regular data, and naively converting events to dense arrays throws away the sparsity benefit. Espresso is an architecture (implemented on an FPGA — a reprogrammable chip) that processes event streams while keeping the data sparse throughout, using ordered data structures and compute patterns tailored to the irregular, event-driven nature of the input. The goal is to run event-camera algorithms faster and with less energy than dense-frame alternatives. Details on exact speedups and the specific vision tasks targeted are not confirmed from the abstract alone.
